However, while interacting with them over the following few days, Hathor gradually realized that the relationships between the five of them weren't as smooth as expected. The Mentor and Jenson, who were familiar with her, could sense her true thoughts from her expressions and actions even when she said nothing, and knew she wasn't intentionally cold. The two new members didn't seem to understand, though. Perhaps due to her icy exterior, they always showed some instinctive wariness, completely different from how lively they were when facing the Mentor. Just as Hathor was repeatedly pondering how to explain to them that she simply wasn't good at socializing, a conversation with the Mentor changed everything. She was given a unique commission: spend time with Haniel and Illica, and understand the lives of modern youngsters. This was a task with a clear directive, so she didn't hesitate.

However, when actually facing the two, taking the initiative to speak proved much more difficult than expected. Hathor had mentally rehearsed scenarios for initial conversations many times and had even prepared several backup plans for dealing with awkward silences. So, during a rare chat session, she tentatively asked about their daily hobbies. The following responses completely deviated from her expectations:
"Of course it's watching the greatest manga of this century, 'Gen Z'!"
"Buying merch, going to events, analyzing the lore with fellow fans on Bagel, conventions, live events, and wotagei!"
"Seasonal anime previews, fan arts, weekly new episodes… we never miss a single one!"
Faced with Haniel's enthusiastic string of recommendations, Hathor showed visible confusion: What is wotagei? What is an "anime"?
Just as Hathor was about to interrupt and give her brain some time to process, she caught sight of Illica, who was eagerly waiting with excitement to join the conversation. She fell silent for a moment and held herself back from speaking. If they'd really like to talk about it… then listening for a while longer wouldn't hurt.
在所有的姐妹中，唯有一位，残虹在与之对视时，会克制住自己的异能。\r\n也唯有这:
Among all her sisters, only one made Zankou limit her abilities when they locked eyes.
Her soul was a pure, translucent flame, as clear as the first light of dawn. As if beholding a wondrous sight, she blurted out at their very first meeting…
"What a beautiful color…"
But the white-clad girl named Daffodill didn't understand. She simply obeyed her adoptive mother's orders, walked to the car door, bowed, and reached out to welcome her new little sister.
"Welcome home, little sister."
Zankou reached out toward her, obsession and curiosity gathering in her eyes. Unknowingly, a feral smile nearly surfaced on the girl's face. As if snatching something away, she suddenly clutched that girl's hand tightly, pulling her closer, as if wanting to bathe herself in that hallowed flame…
After that unconventional greeting, they were eventually ordered to become partners, sisters—family.
Zankou knew she and her sister were not the same, but so what? Two complete opposites—conjoined in their fate. In the Scarlet Letter Garden, countless vines would wind around and bind them, till death did them part. They would step into the same mire, share the same flower bed, walk onto the same battlefield, and return to the same grave. They were as close as family could be.
Day after day, she watched Daffodill through her "special" eye. As the first daughter adopted by Inanna, Daffodill was steadfast and immovable, rigid—no matter how harsh the mission, she would always surpass Mother's expectations. When it came to eliminating a target, she was even unfeeling… Yet that very same sister would tenderly heal her wounds after every mission or punishment.
…But later, for some undiscernable reason, Daffodill changed. That decisiveness and indifference became hesitation, along with growing melancholy and confusion. From then on, that white, steady flame would occasionally flutter.
"So she has a side like that too, then."
Zankou continued to observe Daffodill, as though watching a bud begin to blossom. If her sister became weak, before Mother destroyed and discarded her, she would transform her into her most prized possession. With a heavy heart, Zankou looked forward to that day.
母亲没有死于姐姐的暗杀，她醒来，养好伤，仿佛无事发生一般保持着平日里的形象。残虹:
Mother survived Daffodill's attempt on her life. She woke, recovered from her injuries, and maintained her usual image as if nothing had occurred. Zankou was unsurprised. Daffodill had mastered the art of assassination, but someone like Mother was not to be trifled with. She still performed her role as that poised, luxurious philanthropist—as if entirely unphased by Daffodill's betrayal.
Zankou could see the subtle change, however.
In the past, Mother's emotions had always been stable and cold, even going so far as to be utterly arrogant. Following the assassination attempt, though, she became distrustful, constantly carrying the unease often found in those in positions of power…
The scarlet tower in her memory had already collapsed, but Zankou no longer cared about such frivolous things.
Right now, her only desire was to drag that woman who had slipped through her fingers back by the neck…
Mother brought another "Little Sister" back home, eventually. She had begun to favor the children whose vulnerability made her feel powerful in turn—and the girl named Poinsette was one of them. At first, Zankou only considered her another flower among the field. Unexpectedly, though, she discovered an interesting side to the newly introduced bud. Precocious and gifted, that little bud wouldn't let Mother's favoritism or torment transform her into a wilting flower. Instead, she became a resilient weed, seeking any way of escape from Scarlet Letter's garden. Seeing through her act, Zankou became even more curious and took the initiative to entice Mother into promoting Poinsette, so that she would serve at Inanna's side from then on. That little bud, now a weed, noticed Zankou's intentions, and could only obediently play along…
Though the song and dance between the two amused Zankou for a while, it couldn't fill the void left by Daffodill's absence. Zankou never encountered anyone whose soul could compare to hers, and thus her longing grew day by day…
At last, after a long and thorough investigation, she caught wind of Daffodil's trail—a rundown antique shop in Hethereau, a shanty utterly unfit for her.
Fortunately, Inanna's next target was also in Hethereau, so Zankou gladly undertook the mission and went to investigate. Daily, she disguised herself as various passersby, passing by Eibon's door countless times, until she had finally come upon the face she had waited so long to see.
Suppressing a smile, she slipped into a dark alley, pressed a hand to her chest, and felt her heartbeat pounding wildly like a drum.
"This time, you'll never escape from me again, Sister."
残虹鲜少提起她来到「红字」之前的经历，于她而言，那段幽暗的时光并不值得回顾。\n:
Zankou rarely speaks of the days that came before she joined The Scarlet Letter. To her, such dark times were not worth remembering.
It all began with a careless, secret experiment. A solitary, unknown girl was treated as a vessel for cultivating Esper Ability, and the researchers, along with those greedy, gluttonous elites, considered her a worthless sacrifice on the path to greatness. Unbelievable pain, solitude, mutilation, rebirth… these grotesque, repulsive torments were daily occurrences. Time and again, she would inch towards the edge of death, only to be dragged back to the world of the living.
Until, in a bitter irony, a miracle truly came to pass: her Esper Ability burst forth, turning that sinful dungeon into an ocean of blood. No one survived but her.
A noble, pure-hearted philanthropist was the first to discover her amidst the ruins. She brought that girl back to the gardens, as if transporting a feral wildflower. To her delight, that wildflower, born in the filth and muck, was already tempered completely—exactly to her liking.
Thus, the flower known as "Red Nightshade" took root in the soil of Scarlet Letter, and Inanna gained her loyal adopted daughter—her sharpest dagger.
Yet, Inanna was unaware that the "leash" on her daughter frayed at the edges. Zankou kept quiet about her own Esper Ability, and only opened that uncanny eye of hers from the shadows, hoping to peer into her new family's hearts. Those who tried to bully her, curry favor, or befriend, were merely ignored—and instead swept into a sinking mire, where reality and illusion blurred. They began to doubt what was real or false, slowly transforming into soulless husks—playthings to be puppeteered by Zankou.
"Everyone has a flame burning in their heart."
To Zankou, people's faces were merely monochrome, but the bright red flames of their souls never ceased to burn.
Each person's fire was different—some fierce, some dim, some dark, some crimson… In her eyes, most were utterly mundane; the few that were worth a second glance could only serve as brief playthings. It was only when she watched those flames burn themselves out on the brink of collapse, exhaling flake after flake of hopeless ash, that she showed a hint of delight, as if at last admiring a masterpiece.
But in this cold, monotonous world, dotted with countless dreary flickers, there was always one different soul… At first, it was a blinding white; later, it became a hue she had yet to see anywhere else—an indescribable color.
"How beautiful… I'm unable to look away."
「我的爸爸和妈妈都是异能者。」\n灵可初次谈及家属的情况时，把管理局的档案管理员:
"My mom and dad are both Espers."
The first time Linko talked about her family, she scared the Bureau's archivist half to death, because they'd already checked—her parents were perfectly normal—or at least, in Hethereau, normal people with no Esper abilities.
But then she further explained that her "Dad's Esper Ability is sitting perfectly still through more than a dozen movies in a row," and her "Mom's Esper Ability is walking more than a dozen street blocks without stopping," causing everyone to let out a sigh of relief. Afterwards, they immediately started gossiping about how such amazing people could've ended up together.
Linko's mother was an urban exploration blogger—an endlessly energetic go-getter who believed in ghosts, urban legends, UFOs, aliens, and just about every other paranormal thing you could think of. Every day she'd trawl forum posts for leads, and the moment she thought, "This might be a real one!" she'd set off to investigate… Of course, most of the time her impulsiveness got her fooled by those half-baked posts and she'd end up empty-handed, but she never let such things discourage her. Eventually, she really did stumble into a legitimate spooky spot… and subsequently fell into an Anomalous Realm. There, she met another unlucky soul: a film nerd obsessed with supernatural movies, stuck in a creative rut, who'd shut himself away for days to research new creative ideas before deciding on that spot to shoot his new project.
And so, a very Hethereau kind of love story began. Two young people whose personalities were complete opposites met in the Anomalous Realm. At first, they couldn't stand each other, but then later helped each other, stayed together, escaped danger alongside each other, kept thinking about each other, and finally, the next time they ran into each other, confessed their feelings. Linko has heard that story from them both many-a-time, along with plenty of conflicting versions—but the one thing that never changed was their continual adoration for each other.
After Linko was born, those two young Hethereau parents poured all their love into her, and thus she inherited their quirks, too. The first time their daughter crawled into the bedroom with a pacifier in her mouth, Dad generously shared one of his treasured finds—his carefully edited, age-appropriate supernatural movies… And just like that, before she had even outgrown her bottle, Linko could watch horror flicks with her father without batting an eye. Not long after she learned to walk, Mom would take her out to practice, only to get distracted by some shop she'd never been to before and somehow end up walking up and down the entire city block… Strange as all that sounds, whenever Linko talks about her mom and dad, she wears the same happy smile they do.
In any case, little Linko grew up bathed in love.

十岁那年，灵可时常跟着电波，独自在城市里到处乱走。在途中感受未知的电波，循着电波:
When Linko was ten, she would often follow frequencies and wander all over the city by herself. Feeling out unknown frequencies and exploring wherever they led became her own private, joyful way of passing the time—even if her adventures usually only turned up strange little things, and sometimes even led her to dangerous Anomalies, Linko never got tired of it.
One afternoon, Linko sensed a warm, welcoming frequency, full of an energetic, life-filled energy. She followed its direction, passing through streets and alleys, turning several corners, and even climbing a big tree, all under the frequency's guidance.
She was small, however, and the trunk was huge. She ran out of strength halfway up the tree. Stuck there with nowhere to go, she could only curl up and think of a way out of her situation. Suddenly, a girl in a Clement Academy uniform jumped down from a higher branch and helped her down, all while saying things like, "What were you thinking, climbing a tree this high all by yourself?"
"I'm playing Tamachi GO. I thought I could catch a Rare Tamachi up in the tree, but instead… I only caught you! Here, let me show you my Tamachi Index…"
"Huh?! That really is a Rare Tamachi! You must be a genius at this sort of thing!"
A gentle, kind frequency came from the girl. Like a sunflower basking in the sun. Linko brightened up too.
After that, Linko often went exploring all over the city with her newfound sister-figure, and she started collecting her own Tamachi Index too. She always searched for Tamachi purely by instinct. Even though it got her into plenty of trouble from time to time, the joy of pet-hunting outweighed it all. Still, her Index never quite caught up to her sister's.
Two years later, her sister became busy with school and handed her beloved console and handwritten strategy notes over to Linko, asking her to inherit her Tamachi Index and become a Tamachi Master for the both of them.
"Linko is the best guide in all of Hethereau. Believe in yourself—your path is the right path!"
That was what Linko's sister had said to her the last time they met.
After that, Linko kept exploring the city, squeezing into every nook and cranny to catch Tamachi. She still got lost often, but in the end, she always found her way back home. Every time she caught a new Tamachi, she compared her own Index with her sister's, only to find that her sister had already collected it. Nevertheless, Linko didn't lose heart. She just kept searching, believing that one day her Index would catch up to her sister's and even surpass it.
But from then on, every time she caught a Tamachi, Linko never again felt that same warm, lively frequency.
"So the source of that frequency was my sister all along…"
灵可的异能觉醒于七岁。\n那是一个再寻常不过的傍晚，妈妈带着灵可在超市中闲逛，顺:
Linko's Esper Abilities awakened at the young age of seven.
It was an utterly ordinary evening. Linko's mother had taken her along on a stroll through the supermarket, picking up holiday snacks and decorations while they were out. Linko followed her mother, yet her gaze drifted to a peculiar shop down the street. When she snapped back into reality, her mother had vanished entirely. The crowd was gone too, along with the surrounding noise, leaving her alone in an empty mall. At the time, she was too young to understand what an Anomalous Realm was. Initially, Linko had only wanted to escape that strange maze so that she could find her mother. The space itself was seemingly infinite, however. Linko called out in a faint little voice and cried, with no idea where to go. Hours later, exhausted, she fell to the floor, with almost nothing left but a plea on her lips…
"If only I could find Mom and Dad."
As if answering that wish, all at once, countless loud "voices" surged in from beyond, flooding the empty mall, then spiraling inward like a vortex and forcing their way into her mind: confused, wary, uncertain, worried, lonely, sirens, barking dogs, singing, ragged breathing… and her mother.
Driven by instinct, her young, exhausted body pushed itself back to its feet. Among the countless invisible threads of sounds, she followed the warmest, most familiar one and continued walking.
Farther. Just a little farther.
The "voices" grew louder and louder, and more and more noises poured into her mind. She could no longer think straight. She could only continue to walk—
Linko could barely remember how she escaped. She only knew that when she opened her eyes again, her tearful parents were holding her tight, and the unfamiliar people in uniforms nearby sighed in relief.
Linko later learned that after she was drawn into an Anomalous Realm, the Bureau dispatched the Containment Units to intervene and rescue her. What she didn't know was that as soon as search personnel confirmed the exit, everyone present suddenly felt as if they were hearing an imaginary, chaotic uproar. Electronic communications briefly went down, and some people even claimed they were seeing double, or that they heard the same voice from multiple directions at once. The incident itself severely disrupted the rescue operation. The Bureau had even suspected that an Esper was the cause, and had already prepared to send in ETD for investigation. But then, all of a sudden, Linko stepped out of the Anomalous Realm on her own. The instant she heard her mother calling out to her, she froze, and the noise disturbing everyone else stopped immediately. The Bureau members on site glanced at one another.
"The trapped citizen is safe and rescued. Victim is a suspected Esper. As for the target Anomaly… Nullification confirmed."
完成员工基础培训后，小吱在粉爪银行的第一份工作是「让顾客办一张卡」。\n「很简单:
After completing basic employee training, Chiz's first task at Pink Paws Bank was to get a customer to sign up for a card.
"It's easy," said Mayu, her mentor, patting her on the shoulder. "Our bank has the best benefits in all of Hethereau. You've got this."
"Sorry, I don't need one."
"No thank you."
"Uh-huh, okay, okay, uh-huh, okay, I understand, okay, okay."
Chiz collected dozens of polite refusals and cold shoulders. The air conditioning blasted in the bank lobby; Chiz felt cold inside, too. She huddled in a corner, wondering about resigning. Maybe she wasn't cut out for this job. She was always bad at so many things. She didn't even know how to write a resignation letter.
Chiz would probably remember the day she met Kolinsna forever, with her beautiful golden hair and dazzling red dress. Chiz felt like she was looking at Fons herself walking among mortals. She remembered how Mayu had described it: "Someone who looks like they'd definitely sign up for a card." Chiz really wanted to stay. She just had to try a little harder. So she gathered her courage and walked up. "H-Hello!" she started, "Welcome to Pink Paws Bank… Would you like to sign up for a card?"
The girl with the golden hair and red dress seemed startled by her. She stared at Chiz for a good while, then spoke. Her voice was lovely… until she proceeded to point out Chiz's every flaw; from the way she talked, to her outfit and appearance, to her posture and the angle she was standing at. Chiz felt stares coming from every direction. Tears were already welling up in her eyes. She really wasn't suited for this job after all…
"I'll sign up for a card."
Would Mayu teach her how to write a resignation letter…?
"Hey, don't you even know how to process a card?"
"S-sorry!" Chiz apologized on reflex, then kept responding yes, over and over. Before her brain could catch up, she was already standing in front of the machine. Somehow, despite her fumbling, she managed to successfully issue a card.
"Th-thank you for coming." She didn't know why things had turned out this way, but the result was delightful. After seeing off the young noblewoman, Mayu finally found her chance to approach. She looked at Chiz, who was especially happy about successfully signing up her first customer, with an indescribable expression. "Chiz, do you know who that was?"
"She was… That lady just now?"
"She's the Dvořák family's young lady."
Chiz's smile slowly faded. Pink Paws Bank belonged to the Dvořáks.
Under Mayu's pitying gaze, Chiz choked out: "M-Mayu, do you know how to write a resignation letter?"

After completing basic employee training, Chiz's first task at Pink Paws Bank was to get a customer to sign up for a card.
"It's easy," said Mayu, her mentor, patting her on the shoulder. "Our bank has the best benefits in all of Hethereau. You've got this."
"Sorry, I don't need one."
"No thank you."
"Uh-huh, okay, okay, uh-huh, okay, I understand, okay, okay."
Chiz collected dozens of polite refusals and cold shoulders. The air conditioning blasted in the bank lobby; Chiz felt cold inside, too. She huddled in a corner, wondering about resigning. Maybe she wasn't cut out for this job. She was always bad at so many things. She didn't even know how to write a resignation letter.
Chiz would probably remember the day she met Kolinsna forever, with her beautiful golden hair and dazzling red dress. Chiz felt like she was looking at Fons herself walking among mortals. She remembered how Mayu had described it: "Someone who looks like they'd definitely sign up for a card." Chiz really wanted to stay. She just had to try a little harder. So she gathered her courage and walked up. "H-Hello!" she started, "Welcome to Pink Paws Bank… Would you like to sign up for a card?"
The girl with the golden hair and red dress seemed startled by her. She stared at Chiz for a good while, then spoke. Her voice was lovely… until she proceeded to point out Chiz's every flaw; from the way she talked, to her outfit and appearance, to her posture and the angle she was standing at. Chiz felt stares coming from every direction. Tears were already welling up in her eyes. She really wasn't suited for this job after all…
"I'll sign up for a card."
Would Mayu teach her how to write a resignation letter…?
"Hey, don't you even know how to process a card?"
"S-sorry!" Chiz apologized on reflex, then kept responding yes, over and over. Before her brain could catch up, she was already standing in front of the machine. Somehow, despite her fumbling, she managed to successfully issue a card.
"Th-thank you for coming." She didn't know why things had turned out this way, but the result was delightful. After seeing off the young noblewoman, Mayu finally found her chance to approach. She looked at Chiz, who was especially happy about successfully signing up her first customer, with an indescribable expression. "Chiz, do you know who that was?"
"She was… That lady just now?"
"She's the Dvořák family's young lady."
Chiz's smile slowly faded. Pink Paws Bank belonged to the Dvořáks.
Under Mayu's pitying gaze, Chiz choked out: "M-Mayu, do you know how to write a resignation letter?"

Humans, Anomalies, and everything else all possess a singular, universal truth—a drive to be perceived; like flocks of birds flashing their feathers, flowers giving off aromas, whales singing into the deep… But beyond that, there's something at our core, something even more uniquely our own, spreading outward from body and mind, crossing the thickest barriers and the deepest voids, ceaselessly proving our existence and uniqueness to the universe.
"Like… a 'frequency,' only tuned differently."
When Linko was having her Esper ability information registered, nearly everyone who dealt with her was left more confused than they started. Nothing the girl described could be verified by any device or theory, and yet they all stated at some point that they could clearly feel—if only for a moment—that they were being connected with, as if resonating on the same frequency as something else… Until Linko would say something she really shouldn't in that innocent, caring, faintly sympathetic voice of hers, and they would hurriedly put their dependable adult masks back on.
"Work's really rough, huh… Why not just jump ship?"
"Cough, cough! No, I can't. And I wasn't even thinking about such things. Next question—"

In the early days after her Esper ability awakened, Linko would often be left dizzy after syncing up with too many frequencies at once—causing her to send the noise flooding into her mind back out again unconsciously, disrupting nearby equipment and people. As a result, the Bureau custom-built a head-mounted device for her to help block out interference and to help her focus. Most people her age might have found its design a little intimidating, but Linko loved it. After her ability awakened, the things she liked—and the reasons she liked them or was drawn to them—only became harder for others to understand, which made it even harder for her to fit in. Fortunately, for a loner like Linko, "not being understood" was never a problem that needed solving.
And yet, one accident long ago introduced her to a new companion, and one act of courage landed her a new responsibility. After facing off against the gloomy, taciturn ETD-6 captain, Linko was approved to become the Guarantor for the Oddity Xiaozhen and was brought into ETD-6 as its youngest member due to a special exception. Exe's judgment was spot-on: Linko's Esper Ability made it far easier for ETD-6 to track down and capture Anomaly-related criminals. Whether it was truly frequencies guiding her, or merely the universe putting her on the right path, Linko's uncanny intuition was vital to cracking major cases regardless. Even so, even after a year in ETD, many people still can't help but worry about her wildly offbeat way of doing things.
"…Um, Linko, aren't we a little too far from the main group?"
"Don't worry. It's the main group that's lost. Trust my intuition!"

远离了舞台，也远离了形形色色的异象委托，海月变得无所事事。除了日常起居与复健训练:
Away from the stage and all kinds of Anomaly Commissions, Aurelia found herself with nothing much to do. The thread that had always pulled her forward suddenly snapped. Aurelia had lost her direction all at once. 
She used to think about the future: "Lines" would become the band best at dealing with anomalies and the best at playing music among anomaly hunter organizations… They would leave Hethereau, go on tour, and become legends! When it came to the imagination, there was no such thing as a "limit." But now, nothing seemed to matter anymore.
To pass the boredom of being in the hospital, Aurelia started helping a busy elderly woman in the same ward as her with paperwork. Before being discharged, the old woman extended an invitation: "how about continuing to help out at my business?"
…That didn't seem like a bad idea. It wasn't like she had anywhere else to go anyway.

As if bidding farewell to everything she knew, Aurelia began a brand new life on Tamamochi Street. Not far from StarSign, she became an ordinary part-time office worker.
The street itself was lively, with people constantly coming and going. She knew she had once been a member of the band "Lines," but most residents knew absolutely nothing about her. For the current Aurelia, none of that mattered much anymore. Adults appreciated her professionalism, whereas children thought her riding around on jellyfish was the coolest thing in the world. Before she knew it, she had become "Little" or "Big Sister" Aurelia.
Only once in a while did she muster the courage to take a detour after work and visit StarSign. But, when she reached the steps she had once bounced down endlessly with excitement, she realized: her jellyfish was too big to squeeze down that long, narrow staircase.
The door to the past had permanently closed on her, and she could never go back. The words left unsaid, and tears left unshed, were all that remained in her heart.
She absolutely wished to see Akane and Suzuha again. To hear Akane's song, and see Suzuha's smile—yet she felt that if she ever uttered such a thing out loud, that tiny wish would warp into some kind of curse.
At the very least, she would allow herself to go to every "Night of Moondog"—an Anomalous Realm vast enough to hold all the songs and dreams in the world, or at least one big enough to accommodate one jellyfish. She scanned the list of songs each time she visited, searching for familiar names, only to be disappointed again and again. But, no matter what, Aurelia believed that someday, that little girl born for music would return.
都说遗忘也是成长的一部分。长大后的大人们，大都对儿时只剩下些模模糊糊，像被套上某:
They say forgetting is part of growing up. Most adults only retain hazy fragments of their childhood memories, as if viewing them through some kind of fuzzy filter that makes everything impossible to see clearly.

Edgar is different. With enough effort, he can recall every single day with perfect clarity.

The day Edgar’s family discovered his esper ability went like this:

Edgar was three years old. It was an ordinary evening, no different from any other. His parents had just come home from work, and they were enjoying family time around the dinner table. Light, delicious dishes accompanied by Dad's interesting little anomaly stories made for the perfect cozy atmosphere.

Both of Edgar's parents were clerks at Yggash Court. They were responsible for writing and maintaining anomaly profiles, so Dad always had endless stories to tell. The stories were little tales adapted from the publicly available anomaly profiles he wrote during work hours.

But young Edgar didn't know any of this yet. Whenever Dad got carried away telling stories at the dinner table, he'd look down to see his precious son's bright, sparkling eyes gazing up at him…

Being worshipped by his son as the "Story King" made all those overtime hours worth it.

"That's strange? It seems different from what Dad wrote in the files? Which one is actually true?"

Something changed forever the moment Edgar asked this serious question. Edgar's dad would probably remember that instant for the rest of his life. But his dad quickly focused on something more crucial: how did Edgar know about the anomaly profiles he'd just filed?

Had his son snuck out through the window and run all the way to Yggash Court to read the files? Did such a small child even have clearance to access those documents?

Over the next half hour, Mom and Dad finally figured out what was happening: Edgar only needed to focus his imagination (both adults also had to stretch their own imaginations to picture this) to connect with various libraries around the world, including Yggash Court's archive. Edgar had probably been too curious about what Dad had written, and couldn't help thinking about his father's name… One by one, the anomaly profiles bearing Edgar's father's signature unfolded in Edgar's mind…

By the way, Edgar had discovered this ability long ago. It was probably innate, right? It's just that earlier on, he couldn't read very well, so he couldn't understand all those dense markings on the white papers…

Edgar had probably already read through his father's early work files, when his writing style was still immature. His dad’s "dark history" was now completely exposed to his son. With this realization, Edgar's dad decided to escape to the kitchen to wash dishes, planning to study his son's esper ability more carefully later.

"This child really takes after me. On the night of our first date, I also read through all your papers from cover to cover."

His wife wouldn’t let him off the hook either.

与明音和铃羽成为朋友，是在一次学校组织的春游里。海月盯着水族馆里的水母看得出神，:
Aurelia became friends with Akane and Suzuha on a springtime school trip. She was totally entranced by the jellyfish at the aquarium and, before she knew it, drifted away from the rest of her class's group. Just when she began to panic because she couldn't find a familiar face in the crowd, Akane and Suzuha spotted her. Each of them took one of her hands and led her back to the class rendezvous point, then sat on either side of her on the bus ride home.
From that embarrassing moment onwards, Akane and Suzuha became Aurelia's best friends. 

On the birthday that followed, Aurelia's living room wasn't empty anymore. In front of the incredible gift pile, two girls who'd never seen anything like it merely stared, wide-eyed. "What are you two doing, hiding over there?" The moment they heard Aurelia's voice, Akane immediately tried to shove the tiny present in her hands behind her back. But Aurelia, sharp-eyed as ever, caught her in the act.
"Is that for me? It has to be for me, right?!" Aurelia darted over, making an effort to grab the little box.
"You already have so many presents! T-this one really isn't anything special…"
"That doesn't matter!" Aurelia shouted, full of indignation. She finally managed to get a hold of the gift, hugging it to her chest. "This is my first-ever birthday present from a friend. It's mine, no takebacks!"
"Really… it's nothing…" Akane's voice grew quiet. 
Before she could finish, Aurelia had already ripped the wrapping paper to shreds. Out of the palm-sized box rolled out a few shiny little pins: souvenirs from that same aquarium where they'd first met. The tiny jellyfish mascot wore a cutesy, pitiful expression that, funnily enough, looked like Aurelia when she couldn't stop crying that day. 
Aurelia stared, unblinking, at the pins that had rolled onto the table. Beside her, Akane was so embarrassed she couldn't bear to stay a second longer. She grabbed Suzuha's hand and began to make a move for the door—but before they could even take a step, Aurelia barreled into both of them and wrapped them in a tight hug. The little crybaby was sobbing like the mascot on that pin again. "T-this is perfect… the best thing in the entire world!" She could barely get the words out between her tears.

Even though her parents still couldn't be there for that birthday in particular, Aurelia no longer felt lonely. Suzuha lit the cake candles for her, and Akane set a party hat on her head. The birthday song they sang for her became the most beautiful melody Aurelia had ever heard.
When she blew out the candles, she prayed with all her might that she'd be with these friends of hers forever.

九原领回因异能失控被管理局带走的哈索尔，是多方协调后的结果。失控并非关键，重要的:
It took Jiuyuan a lot of effort to retrieve Hathor after she was taken by the Bureau for losing control of her Esper Abilities. The loss of control itself wasn't the issue. What mattered was how Hathor handled the aftermath, and this was the first lesson Jiuyuan, as Hathor's mentor, needed to teach.
From that day on, Hathor doubled her training regimen on her own. Her movements grew faster and her decisions sharper as she shed off exhaustion for stability. Her expression remained calm, but her rhythm had become erratic. Jiuyuan knew this state all too well: the more one rushes to control one's powers, the easier it becomes for the powers to control them. She didn't stop Hathor’s training, nor did she warn her about overdoing it. Some students tend to mistake reminders for warnings or interpret concern as mentors thinking they aren’t trying hard enough. Rather than have Hathor quietly use such warnings as a new benchmark to push even harder, Jiuyuan thought it was better to let her train where she could watch. By keeping an eye on things, nothing would go wrong.
But the nature of Sterry's work meant Jiuyuan couldn't have Hathor's back forever. How could she pave the way before letting go? What she hadn't expected was that the solution would find its way to her. Haniel, who had stumbled onto the scene when Hathor lost control, unexpectedly had the ability to calm her. And as luck would have it, the girl was also interested in courier work…
Things just fell into place.

Hathor's execution and combat abilities were impeccable, but interacting with others left her at a loss. When the two little owlets first arrived, Hathor faced them like someone flipping through a book with no instructions: cautious, yet clueless about where to begin. The awkwardness in the shop didn't elude Jiuyuan. In a rare move, she gave Hathor a special commission: make an effort to understand today's youth and assimilate.
Imagining the ever-methodical Hathor carrying out this commission, Jiuyuan, who was usually so adept at controlling her emotions, couldn't suppress a smile—her first one.
What Jiuyuan had always known, but Hathor had yet to realize: that stubborn, almost clumsy honesty of hers, was exactly what she needed to connect with those two little owlets.

Changes began to occur in Hathor’s daily life: popular comics started appearing on her desk, and on days off, she would go to livehouses with Haniel and Illica instead of staying alone in the training room. Occasionally, new words she'd never used before would slip into her conversations.
Though Hathor still worried about losing control, much of her tension had vanished amidst the laughter and playfulness of everyday life at Sterry. After one Esper control lesson, Jenson, who had been watching, teased, "You've been mentoring her for so long, and now she's getting more popular thanks to being 'led astray' by those two little owlets. How does that feel?"
"I thought you only cared about fishing. Seems you haven't completely lost your sense as a spy."
Hathor's tone was as flat as ever: "Would you like me to conduct another loss-of-control test right now?"
Jiuyuan glanced at Jenson, who was silently calculating the renovation costs if Hathor decided to lose control on purpose. Jiuyuan couldn't help but smile. "No need. Things are just fine the way they are."
There's no need to mold a student to fit some standard. She can find her own answer.

"I thought you only cared about fishing. Seems you haven't completely lost your sense as a spy."
Hathor's tone was as flat as ever: "Would you like me to conduct another loss-of-control test right now?"
Jiuyuan glanced at Jenson, who was silently calculating the renovation costs if Hathor decided to lose control on purpose. Jiuyuan couldn't help but smile. "No need. Things are just fine the way they are."

海月的异能在十四岁时觉醒。具体是什么场合发生的事，她自己也搞不清楚——第一次发现:
Aurelia's Esper ability awakened when she was fourteen. She couldn't remember exactly what was going on at the time, except that one time, when she was writing in class, her pen ran out of ink. Just as she gave her pen a shake, an entire school of jellyfish suddenly appeared. Both the teachers and students lost their trains of thought completely upon seeing this, their eyes wide and jaws to the floor. 
In the middle of the crowd, Aurelia was the most confused of all. "I just… did this?"
She tried shaking her hand again. The jellyfish mimicked her hand movements perfectly. Her classmates shouted in excitement, "Aurelia! Are you, like… did you just become…"
"You're an Esper!"

After many tests, it was officially confirmed that Aurelia was indeed an Esper now. But, aside from registering her status at the Bureau of Anomaly Control, her life didn't seem to change at all—until she realized the price she had to pay for it.
Losing her sense of direction turned Aurelia into a stranger in her own hometown. Though she walked the same route to and from school every day, she would forget where she was at any point again and again. The shops along the road all looked familiar, but when it came time to cross the street or turn a corner, her mind drew a complete blank. From then on, no matter where she had to go, Aurelia had to look up the route in advance and memorize every detail. 
Initially, everyone at her school thought Espers were super powerful and cool. They looked at Aurelia with envy and awe. But it turned out that Aurelia's Esper ability was pretty underwhelming. What situation would ever occur where someone needed to summon and control jellyfish? It was entirely useless. It didn't take long for their excitement about her being an Esper to die down, and instead, focus on her daily navigation disasters. Even though the classmates who knew about her condition did their best to look out for her on campus, the moment a shop changed its sign or some road got closed down for construction, Aurelia would end up scrambling around, asking anyone and everyone for directions. In the end, Akane and Suzuha got into the habit of going out of their way to pick Aurelia up and drop her off every day, terrified of her wandering around in the streets in the middle of the night. 
"I don't want to keep bothering you with stuff like this…" Aurelia muttered, her head hanging low. Suzuha held Aurelia's hand, giving it a little tug, signaling that they needed to turn left at the intersection. Walking alongside them, Akane let out a sigh. She lifted her hand and flicked Aurelia on the forehead. Aurelia shrank back, exclaiming, "Ow! That hurt, you know!"
"You became an Esper, that's all. You haven't changed as a person. You've always been a hassle, even since you were little!"
Suzuha burst out laughing next to them. Aurelia puffed out her cheeks in protest, "Akane! You're so mean…"
"Am I wrong? H-Hey! Stay back!"

Warmed by her friends' laughter, Aurelia let the topic go. However, though she stayed sunny and optimistic on the surface, a tiny bit of unease had gripped her heart.
Am I truly the same as before? Can things really stay the same between us?

小吱站在金碧辉煌的银行大厅里，穿着得体又漂亮；\n小吱走在路灯照不到的角落，翘起:
Chiz stands, professionally dressed, in the gleaming lobby of a bank.
Chiz walks the corners where the streetlights don't reach, sewage pooling under the cracks in the pavement.
"Chiz, Chiz, where are you going?"

Once Chiz learned to run without stumbling, she had to leave home and help her older siblings find food outside. Shiny bread wrapped in plastic… Chiz only saw that once. Most of the time, all she could find were wild vegetables and mushrooms. When even those were gone, they had no choice but to hunt "Apocha." That's what they called the edible Anomalies. But Apocha were dangerous; it was common to get hurt, and medicine was even harder to find than food. And then there was that saying: "Eat too many Apocha, and you'll become an Esper." Espers, like Anomalies, were outsiders to be driven away; because, just like Anomalies, Espers attack. After dinner, Chiz watched her mother cradle her newborn baby sister; patting her, soothing her, singing to her. Chiz remembered when she was little, so little that the whole world was no bigger than her mother's embrace, her mother would gently pat her, soothe her, and sing to her.
"Chiz, Chiz, grow up quick."

Faster, faster. Chiz pressed her palm against the bleeding wound on her neck, glancing back at the Apocha that was closely tailing her. She ran as hard as she could, away from home. Farther, farther—until she couldn't run anymore. Chiz tripped on a rock and fell hard to the ground. The Apocha had vanished somewhere along the way. She didn't have the strength to stand, so she just lay there, nibbling at the food she'd found. She could only eat a little. She had to bring the rest home. Her family was waiting for her. She had to get home… Chiz couldn't remember how she found her way back. But somehow, she made it home with the food… and a new Ability. Maybe, just like the stories said, she had eaten too many Apocha. On her last night home, she used her new Esper Ability to put on a little fireworks show for her younger siblings. She remembered their eyes shining bright, their soft gasps; fighting over who got to play with their magical big sister.
The next day, her mother brought Chiz to the shore. A boat would take her away from home, carry her to a new world. Even after her mother's silhouette had completely disappeared from sight, Chiz could still hear someone calling out in the salty sea breeze.
"Chiz, Chiz, you must…"

Chiz now lives in the heart of Hethereau. Even at night, the whole New Herland District blazes with lights. Chiz often turns off all her lights indoors and leans against the window, watching the flow of cars outside. Back in her homeland, nights were deathly silent. Light didn't mean streetlamps or the moon; light meant danger. It could be an Anomaly's lure. It could be dangerous Espers and their weapons.
Chiz sits in the darkness of her room, while a glittering world sparkles outside her window. She hugs herself, imitating her mother from memory, softly humming a melody still warm with feeling.
"Chiz, Chiz, you must be happy."

「外面的世界是危险的。」小吱在很小的时候就知道了这件事，但家里的桌上不会凭空长出:
"The outside world is dangerous." Chiz learned this when she was very young, back when food at home wouldn't just appear on the table. Sometimes, her older siblings would go out and never come back. And then Chiz reached the same age. It was her turn to go outside.
The number of wounds on her body grew faster than her height. The first wound was on her left arm, left by a branch that caught at her while she tried to flee an Anomaly. The second was on her right foot; she stepped in a trap while bumbling down the wrong path through the woods. The third was on her left thigh, where an Apocha bit her before becoming their family's dinner… Some wounds healed and disappeared. Others became scars. The last wound her homeland gave her was on her neck: a scar that remained deep even after healing. In the end, just like her siblings, Chiz went out and never came back.
Chiz boarded a ship headed who knows where; their routes were never fixed, after all. Chiz was unlucky: She became an Esper. But she was lucky enough to find a ship leaving the very next day. All of her mother's love became a thin stack of money pressed into the kind captain's hands. Leave, leave. Staying here will only bring more pain. Chiz began living on the ship with others from her homeland. Some were Espers like her. Others were ordinary people who could no longer bear the strain of staying. But they never really connected, even in such close proximity. One day, two days, three days… One month, two months… Then she lost count. People got on. People got off. The kind captain brought her to a clean, safe city. Chiz was almost landsick.
Chiz arrived at her new home. Here, there were lovely clothes, a warm bed. Delicious food appeared, almost magically, on the table. She sat quietly in a corner, eavesdropping, and learned this was the Dvořák family's orphanage. Chiz loved Dvořák. She loved the orphanage. She made new friends here, and every day they wore the same clothes and ate the same food.
"Why don't you wash your hands?" a friend asked Chiz one evening after dinner. "You should stay clean. You'll trouble the caretakers."
Chiz hid her sauce-stained hands behind her back in alarm. She finally realized that even wearing the same clothes and eating the same food, they were still different. She was a little mouse that had drifted for so long before being being washed ashore here. "Mice are the dirtiest of all!" said the picture books. Of course, her friend was kind. She led Chiz to the bathroom and helped wash the sauce off her hands. Chiz was very grateful.
"You have to wash your hands. If you don't, people won't like you."
Chiz was smart. She remembered this. From then on, she washed her hands spotlessly clean every day. Three rounds of soap. No slacking. Clean between the fingers and under the nails. Wash before bed, wash after waking up, wash before meals, wash after meals, wash before playing with toys, wash after playing with toys… As time went on, just like those old wounds, Chiz's hands became wrapped in bandages. The caretakers cautioned her that she couldn't wash her hands so often. Her friends were worried too, gently blowing on her hands and asking if it hurt. Chiz smiled at all of them. "It doesn't hurt," she promised, saying she'll remember.
Much more time passed. Even after all the wounds on her hands had healed, Chiz still kept the habit of wearing bandages.

「莫非只是沉溺于母亲身份，陶醉这种自我满足？」\n\n【异象故事】\n\n「孩子:
"Could it be that she was merely indulging in the role of mother, intoxicated by self-satisfaction?"

Anomaly Story

"The children will soon hatch, and Mommy has prepared everything."
"Brocade and velvet line the bed, a red silk dreamcatcher keeps nightmares away."
"The children will soon be born, and Mommy has practiced over and over."
"Silver bells go jingle jangle, gentle whispers lull you to sleep."

…

Humming the lullaby over and over, the Mother Bird had waited far, far too long for the day her children would be born. She wished to dote upon them, granting them all the beautiful things in the world. With her mind made up, the Mother Bird spread her wings and left the nest. She journeyed around the world before her eggs hatched, gathering countless treasures. She could see it clearly now: when her children are born, their tender faces would be illuminated by the shimmer of gold and silver filling the nest.
That was the very best a mother could prepare for her children. The Mother Bird was certain of this.
And she, too, would be the very best mother.
Whenever she closed her eyes, her heart was filled with visions of nestling with her hatchlings in a nest woven with golden thread and red silk. She dreamed of gently feeding them, watching them grow up healthy and hearty.

But such a scene would never come to pass.
The Mother Bird, so full of anticipation, never got to become a mother.
When she returned to the nest with a gem-studded mask in her beak, she was devastated to find only shattered eggshells. Her children were nowhere to be found.

Who stole my children!!!
Broke their shells and stole them from their mother!!!
It is said the shrill cries from the nest continued for three days and three nights without end.

From that day on, the Mother Bird ceased to exist. Only a bird-like creature wearing a mask with an expression neither smiling nor crying, the Nestbound Bird, remained there, guarding an eggshell with its cracks mended by red thread.
Any living being in this world could be my stolen child, so I shall be the mother of any living being in this world.
My stolen, lost children. Come back to me. Come back to this beautifully decorated nest.
Mommy promises no one will ever separate us again.
Look at these Plumettes sewn from my bones, my feathers, my flesh. They will forever guard this nest.
Come back. Please, call me Mommy.

Children who grew up in Hethereau have mostly heard this story. When lost, never heed the gentle and loving female voice calling your name from who knows where. If you answer that earnest call, you will be taken back to the Nestbound Bird's nest and raised as its child. If you listen to it and call it "Mommy," you will forget yourself forever, destined to become lost in the nest.

Who exactly stole her children? This question seems destined to remain unanswered, or perhaps the Mother Bird knew the answer all along…
The Mother Bird, so blinded by decorating a comfortable nest for her children, neglected to actually care for and accompany them. The newly hatched chicks could not find their mother and, driven by hunger, had no choice but to leave the nest. Their whereabouts remain unknown.
What does it matter if the truth is simple and clear? The Mother Bird no longer exists.
Only the Nestbound Bird's earnest calls for her children continue to echo.


Anomaly Characteristics
· This Anomaly resembles a giant bird-like creature with its face concealed by a human-faced mask. It generally dwells in an Anomalous Realm it calls its "nest."
· It calls out to lost children in a gentle, loving female voice, then abducts the entranced children to its nest.
· After the Nestbound Bird succeeds, it hangs a mask at the archway of the "nest" entrance, signifying its protection over the abducted child.

Anomaly Nexus
"The identity of mother"

Risk Assessment
Critical risk.

Containment/Guarantee Status
/

Containment Measures
/
升入中学后，灵可依然经常在海特洛闲逛，跟随着各种奇妙电波的指引。一天，她走入了一:
After starting middle school, Linko still often strolled around Hethereau, following the guidance of all kinds of strange frequencies. One day, she went in through the back door of a building and accidentally stumbled into an Anomalous Realm. It was a room with walls that were lined with old TVs, most of them with broken screens that no longer turned on. Following a faint but warm frequency, she searched through the pile of battered old TVs and found one that was very, very small.
Driven by a sudden instinct, Linko pressed the power switch. After a burst of static, a little ghost suddenly popped out.
"Wah!! You unlucky little imp, how dare you disturb this evil spirit's rest! As compensation, starting today, you belong to this evil spirit as its servant! Heh heh heh—mmph—"
Having seen plenty of horror movies, Linko wasn't scared in the slightest. She simply scooped up the little ghost like she was catching a stray cat on any normal day.
"So you were fine, after all. Just a minute ago, your frequency almost disappeared."
"Huh? Frequency? Gone? What kind of nonsense are you spewing? I was just taking a little nap in the TV!"
"You live in a TV… Tamachi live in a screen too, so you're basically like a Tamachi—oh! So you're an electronic pet!"
"Huh? What the hell is that supposed to mean? Who are you calling a pet!? Believe it or not, this evil spirit will mmmph—"
"Yes. From now on, I'll call you Xiaozhen."
After that baffling negotiation, Linko took the little ghost Xiaozhen away… along with her TV.
But when they left the Anomalous Realm, a group of people in Bureau uniforms were already waiting at the entrance for them.
What Linko didn't know at the time was that Xiaozhen had long existed as an Anomaly inside the office building. She could slip into all kinds of TVs and would occasionally pop out to scare employees working late. But on that day, an Esper criminal broke into the building with hopes to cause harm. Just as he was about to attack an innocent employee, they were suddenly dragged into the Anomalous Realm. According to the people who experienced it firsthand, it was a labyrinth made from countless piled-up TVs. They were sealed away in a safe room, while the criminal was confronted by ghostly fire spilling out from countless TV screens, and by a massive ghost formed from those coalescing flames. The battle in the Anomalous Realm lasted for what felt like hours. The ghost's strength was nearly exhausted, and was almost nullified. However, Xiaozhen used the last of her strength to fling the criminal out of the Anomalous Realm. After that, she found the last intact TV and went into a deep slumber… until Linko suddenly woke her again.
In the end, ETD-6 arrested the injured Esper criminal in the empty building. Not long afterward, Linko and the office workers reappeared inside. Fortunately, there were no casualties. Linko and Xiaozhen were investigated by the Bureau following the whole debacle. Linko met a grim-faced young man, and the uniformed personnel seemed to treat him with considerable deference.
"The Celaeno Compound is interested in that ghost."
Linko didn't know what kind of place that was, but her instincts told her it couldn't mean anything good for Xiaozhen. She could vaguely sense that even within the deathly-still frequency of the man before her, there might be a weak point she could utilize…
"Xiaozhen isn't a malicious spirit. I'm not handing her over to you, because…"
Firm and unflinching, Linko clutched the TV with Xiaozhen inside tightly to her chest.
"—she's my friend. I don't want to be separated from her."
"…"
The young man said nothing more. Not long after, Linko received a document. An ETD captain secured the decision that allowed her to keep Xiaozhen. On the condition that she accept ETD oversight and arrangements, she would be permitted to become Xiaozhen's Guarantor.
"Xiaozhen, Xiaozhen! I'm your official Guarantor now!"
"Guarantor? What does that mean?"
"It's not a master and not a servant… um… whatever. The point is, you get to stay with me!"
"…Heh heh heh~ Then this evil spirit shall graciously look after you, little frequency imp!"

升入中学后，灵可依然经常在海特洛闲逛，跟随着各种奇妙电波的指引。一天，她走入了一:
After starting middle school, Linko still often strolled around Hethereau, following the guidance of all kinds of strange frequencies. One day, she went in through the back door of a building and accidentally stumbled into an Anomalous Realm. It was a room with walls that were lined with old TVs, most of them with broken screens that no longer turned on. Following a faint but warm frequency, she searched through the pile of battered old TVs and found one that was very, very small.
Driven by a sudden instinct, Linko pressed the power switch. After a burst of static, a little ghost suddenly popped out.
"Wah!! You unlucky little imp, how dare you disturb this evil spirit's rest! As compensation, starting today, you belong to this evil spirit as its servant! Heh heh heh—mmph—"
Having seen plenty of horror movies, Linko wasn't scared in the slightest. She simply scooped up the little ghost like she was catching a stray cat on any normal day.
"So you were fine, after all. Just a minute ago, your frequency almost disappeared."
"Huh? Frequency? Gone? What kind of nonsense are you spewing? I was just taking a little nap in the TV!"
"You live in a TV… Tamachi live in a screen too, so you're basically like a Tamachi—oh! So you're an electronic pet!"
"Huh? What the hell is that supposed to mean? Who are you calling a pet!? Believe it or not, this evil spirit will mmmph—"
"Yes. From now on, I'll call you Xiaozhen."
After that baffling negotiation, Linko took the little ghost Xiaozhen away… along with her TV.
But when they left the Anomalous Realm, a group of people in Bureau uniforms were already waiting at the entrance for them.
What Linko didn't know at the time was that Xiaozhen had long existed as an Anomaly inside the office building. She could slip into all kinds of TVs and would occasionally pop out to scare employees working late. But on that day, an Esper criminal broke into the building with hopes to cause harm. Just as he was about to attack an innocent employee, they were suddenly dragged into the Anomalous Realm. According to the people who experienced it firsthand, it was a labyrinth made from countless piled-up TVs. They were sealed away in a safe room, while the criminal was confronted by ghostly fire spilling out from countless TV screens, and by a massive ghost formed from those coalescing flames. The battle in the Anomalous Realm lasted for what felt like hours. The ghost's strength was nearly exhausted, and was almost nullified. However, Xiaozhen used the last of her strength to fling the criminal out of the Anomalous Realm. After that, she found the last intact TV and went into a deep slumber… until Linko suddenly woke her again.
In the end, ETD-6 arrested the injured Esper criminal in the empty building. Not long afterward, Linko and the office workers reappeared inside. Fortunately, there were no casualties. Linko and Xiaozhen were investigated by the Bureau following the whole debacle. Linko met a grim-faced young man, and the uniformed personnel seemed to treat him with considerable deference.
"The Celaeno Compound is interested in that ghost."
Linko didn't know what kind of place that was, but her instincts told her it couldn't mean anything good for Xiaozhen. She could vaguely sense that even within the deathly-still frequency of the man before her, there might be a weak point she could utilize…
"Xiaozhen isn't a malicious spirit. I'm not handing her over to you, because…"
Firm and unflinching, Linko clutched the TV with Xiaozhen inside tightly to her chest.
"—she's my friend. I don't want to be separated from her."
"…"
The young man said nothing more. Not long after, Linko received a document. An ETD captain secured the decision that allowed her to keep Xiaozhen. On the condition that she accept ETD oversight and arrangements, she would be permitted to become Xiaozhen's Guarantor.
"Xiaozhen, Xiaozhen! I'm your official Guarantor now!"
"Guarantor? What does that mean?"
"It's not a master and not a servant… um… whatever. The point is, you get to stay with me!"
"…Heh heh heh~ Then this evil spirit shall graciously look after you, little frequency imp!"
「黑猫到来之前，我们一无所有。黑猫到来之后，我们拥有一切。」\n\n【异象故事】:
Before the black cat came, we had nothing. After the black cat came, we had everything.

Anomaly Story
Mammon came into existence long ago, when ancient tribes first began fighting over treasure and territory. The Anomaly's true form is that of a massive black beast, yet it chooses to appear before people as a black cat with golden eyes, adorned with lavish jewelry. It is a omen of desire, with a keen nose that can sniff out the scent of greed. This elegant black cat prowls near wars sparked by avarice, seizing desires to satisfy its bottomless appetite. Besides desire, Mammon also loves to devour money. After all, for thousands of years, humanity has never given up its pursuit and possession of wealth, so the greed attached to coin is often the richest and purest.
In the modern times, conflicts have all but ceased. Once people's basic needs are largely met, the little desire they retain isn't even enough to serve as a snack for Mammon. As the hungry black cat was searching for food, its gaze fell upon the wealthiest family in Hethereau, the Dvořák family, and the Anomaly that could bring infinite wealth, Ladon. Thus, Pink Paws Bank and Gold Apple Collection Hall became the two locations Mammon frequents most. Predictably, the deplorable act of devouring gold coins is absolutely intolerable to Ladon, who views Mammon as a natural enemy. The moment Mammon's trail appears nearby, Ladon will mercilessly drive it away, refusing to stop until Mammon is nullified. To humans, the conflict between these two Anomalies appears to be nothing more than two bad-tempered cats fighting. Before long, their "guardians", representatives of the Dvořák family and members of ETD, will arrive with dried fish and balls of yarn to mediate. This is a common sight to see. Apart from Fons being swallowed by Mammon, their disputes have not caused any real harm to other people or buildings. But from the perspective of the Anomalies, every time they roll up their sleeves and prepare to give the other a good thrashing, some meddlesome humans always show up to watch or break up the fight… This must give both cats quite the headache.
In truth, Mammon may have arrived in this city much earlier than people realize. Several decades ago, a massive and violent beast-type Anomaly suddenly appeared in the central area of Hethereau and attacked nearby residents, causing a great panic. The Bureau of Anomaly Control was urgently dispatched to contain this unknown Anomaly, but it fled after its defeat and its whereabouts became unknown. Personnel involved in the containment conducted a carpet search of the surrounding area but found nothing, with no trace of this monster surfacing again. According to reliable sources, that Anomaly was actually Mammon's true form. After being defeated, it did not leave, choosing instead to wander the streets in the guise of a stray cat. For unknown reasons, its Wertheimer Index fluctuations are extremely low, so the Bureau of Anomaly Control never detected its presence. No one would connect the Fons thief currently running rampant in Hethereau with the black beast that once caused so much trouble… But what brought Mammon to this city in the first place? Why does it truly linger here? The secrets hidden behind those golden eyes may only be uncovered by those who come after…
In my opinion, even if Mammon were to devour the entire Dvořák family's fortune- no, all the wealth in Hethereau, or even the entire world, it would only temporarily appease its insatiable heart. Desire itself can never be truly satisfied. One needs only look back at history: no matter how much desire is fulfilled, new desires will continue to emerge endlessly. Perhaps it is under this powerful catalyst that the wheels of our society keep rolling forward, never ceasing.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Its true form is a massive black beast. Under normal circumstances, it appears as a black cat with golden eyes.
· Feeds on human greed and money. Seems to possess the ability to amplify human desires.

Anomaly Nexus
Giving Mammon what it craves will achieve temporary nullification.

Risk Assessment
Moderate risk. Generally harmless to humans, but since it is impossible to predict when it might go berserk, cautious contact is advised.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Unique Anomaly. Not in containment.

Containment Measures
Not in containment.

Experiment Records
/

Derivative Anomaly
/

Extended Info
/

「大海在流血。」\n\n【异象故事】\n按照最后一次航行报告，裴廓德号当时已经追:
"The sea is bleeding."

Anomaly Story
According to the final voyage report, the Pequod had been chasing a whale for forty days. Supplies were nearly exhausted and the crew was at their mental limit, but the whale they pursued was also on its last legs. Harpoon strikes had caused the great beast to bleed, leaving a red trail across the open ocean. The whale was heading towards a field of packed ice, perhaps hoping to force the Pequod to abandon pursuit. Shortly after, both the whale and the Pequod vanished into the packed ice. No one ever saw them again, until we encountered the Sea Prisoner.

R-1851(Or) Sea Prisoner is a large Bio Anomaly resembling a whale-like creature. According to citizen reports, when traversing the undersea tunnels, one can occasionally hear "strange singing." Continuing forward leads into the Sea Prisoner's Anomalous Realm, which resembles packed ice interspersed with shipwrecks and abandoned structures. Inside this Anomalous Realm, water becomes "walkable." The surface remains liquid, but attempting to go below the surface meets resistance. The water composition is similar to seawater, but a period after the Anomalous Realm forms, it turns a vivid blood red. Though harmless to humans, its appearance is gruesome and terrifying leading frightened drivers to abandon their vehicles and flee. Those who do so soon find themselves exiting the Anomalous Realm, back in the undersea tunnel.
The Sea Prisoner appears unable to leave its Anomalous Realm. Based on certain physical characteristics, the Sea Prisoner shares similarities with the whale the Pequod was tracking, but the Sea Prisoner has many additional growths on its body. Some appear to be characteristics of other marine creatures, while others are scars from healed wounds. A massive harpoon is lodged in the Sea Prisoner's back. It is a common whaling cannon model, but far larger than any standard harpoon. The missing Pequod was equipped with the same model, but we have no way to determine whether this particular harpoon belonged to the Pequod. Nevertheless, after confirming it as a Derivative Anomaly of R-1851(Or), we still gave it the name Pequod.
The Sea Prisoner shows no active aggression, and according to those who have encountered it, the Sea Prisoner initially is friendly and seems inclined to communicate. Unfortunately, no one can understand the Sea Prisoner's singing, so what it is trying to express remained unknown for a long time. After entering the Anomalous Realm, the water eventually turns red and the Sea Prisoner exhibits extreme pain, struggling to dislodge the harpoon deeply embedded in its back. Even without malicious intent, the Sea Prisoner's massive size causes tremendous destruction when it thrashes. After being driven mad by agony, the Sea Prisoner begins attacking everything around it indiscriminately.
Those who have encountered the Sea Prisoner generally report sensing that it is suffering gravely. Having Anomalized, it cannot die, and the harpoon on its back will torment it forever. It appears to draw others into its Anomalous Realm as a cry for help, longing for someone to end its pain. After leaving the Anomalous Realm, those who have encountered the Sea Prisoner generally express concern for its condition. A small number develop obsessive symptoms regarding "helping the Sea Prisoner," but we cannot verify whether these changes stem from post-traumatic stress after witnessing its suffering, or whether the Anomalous Realm exerted influence on their minds.

In nearly all ancient beliefs, the sea was a personified deity: generous yet capricious, an embodiment of abundance and disaster alike. Majestic creatures like whales were also imbued with much mythological significance. Yet now, as reverence for the sea has been replaced by a hunger for resources, few stop to ask: What must we give in return? Will endless plundering one day invite the sea's fury?

Anomaly Characteristics
· The Sea Prisoner is a Bio Anomaly resembling a whale, with characteristics of multiple marine creatures fused together.
· A massive harpoon is lodged in its back, which is a Derivative Anomaly.
· It continuously emits singing of unknown meaning.
· It has no malicious intent, but when affected by the harpoon, it loses reason and attacks everything around it.
· No records exist of it being observed outside its Anomalous Realm, and it is unclear whether this is due to inability or lack of intention.

Anomaly Nexus
The harpoon embedded in the Anomaly's body.

Risk Assessment
Potentially high destructive power, but only within the Anomalous Realm. After entering the Anomalous Realm, getting off the vehicle immediately allows one to leave.

Containment/Guarantee Status
Not in containment. Cannot be guaranteed.

Containment Measures
/

/

海月的腿康复希望非常渺茫，但医生委婉地表示，也并非完全没有恢复部分功能的可能。倘:
Aurelia's chances of recovering the use of her legs were slim, but the doctor gently suggested that it wasn't entirely impossible. If more advanced medical technology emerged in the future, or if she encountered an Esper with profound healing powers…. Regardless, the possibility wasn't zero. 
During the breaks in her rehab, she often opened Bagel and stared at the little group chat with her, Akane, and Suzuha. Neither of them had sent a message to the other in a long, long time. Many times, Aurelia had typed out a message, only to delete it. What was she supposed to say to them?
After countless bouts of agonizing over her phone, Aurelia made up her mind: once she recovered a bit more, to the point where she could be discharged from the hospital and take care of herself, she would go see her friends in person and surprise them. She had endless amounts of things she wanted to tell them about. 

However, even after some time had passed, there was still no improvement in her legs. She had learned to stop treating "recovery" as her only hope. Still, with the help of her Esper Ability, her life gradually returned to some semblance of normalcy. Though she couldn't play the drums like before, Aurelia thought nothing of it. With just a bit more effort, the day of her reunion with Akane and Suzuha wouldn't be far off.
Suddenly, her phone buzzed with a special tone—the one she had set for Akane's messages specifically. Aurelia rushed to grab her phone, nearly fumbling it out of her hands in the process. But, the words that met her eyes once she opened the chat window were ones she never could have imagined: "Suzuha is leaving. By the time she messaged me, her car had already driven off…"
…Huh? 
For a moment, Aurelia couldn't comprehend the meaning of those words, as if they were nothing more than a string of meaningless symbols. What did Akane mean by "leaving"? Why would she say that? Her fingers trembled so much she could barely type out a reply, and a flood of questions sat heavy on the tip of her tongue. 
"Where's Suzuha going?"
She was going somewhere without them. Suzuha wouldn't be staying with them anymore. Aurelia… understood. Suzuha was a sensitive and thoughtful girl. If she kept living in Hethereau, a city filled with memories of their friendship, she would only tear open closed wounds. Aurelia knew this, so there was no need to ask. 
"What about Lines?"
She, deep down, knew the answer to that, too. Even if Suzuha stayed, without Aurelia as their drummer, the band would only have two paths going forward: going on a hiatus or disbanding. Of course, she could recommend something like "find a new drummer," but she couldn't bring herself to say that. "Lines" was born from Aurelia's selfish wish, and it existed for the three of them. If one of them left, what meaning was there in the empty shell left behind? 
"What about you?"

Even through her shaking fingers, she typed out those three words. 
In the chat window, the "someone is typing…" bubble flickered for a long, long time. Akane, who always spoke her mind, must have been desperately searching for words to say, just like Aurelia had done prior. Akane, so straightforward and outspoken, had been pushed beyond her limits.
If it weren't for the fact that Aurelia feared being looked down upon or abandoned, if it weren't for her lack of courage… If it weren't for her…
It felt as though thousands of years had passed before a new message had finally appeared on the screen: "I don't know. I'm sorry."
Aurelia felt herself begin to tremble. The words before her dissolved like paint in water. 
Why? 
Don't disband. 
Weren't we supposed to be together forever? 
Akane loves singing so much—she should always be on stage. 
There was so much Aurelia wanted to say, but she no longer felt she had the right to say it. The one who brought "Lines" to an end, the one who forced Suzuha to leave her hometown, the one who made it so Akane could never sing again… it wasn't fate. It was herself. 
And yet, even so, there was still one thing she wanted to convey. Even if the damage had already been done, even if it was far too late… 

"I love your music, Akane. Please, even if you feel like stopping now, continue it in the future."
"I promise you, I'll definitely be waiting for you wherever you go."

「Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet！」\n\n【异象故事】\:
"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet!"

Anomaly Story
Deep into your desk drawer, you might find a notebook buried among old papers. It probably has a dark cover (most likely cheap synthetic leather), decorated with cryptic symbols or pretentious quotes. Flip through the yellowed pages, and you'll find records of adolescent fantasies, embarrassing incantations you would never want anyone else to see. Most people go through a phase in their teens when they believe they are unique, a chosen one burdened with a special destiny, but they are too self-conscious to tell anyone… and so they stay up late at night, pouring their hearts out to a notebook.
…If you know what I'm talking about, then you probably already have a good idea of what the Anomaly known as the "Black Tome" looks like.

C-7111(Ob) Black Tome typically appears as a book with a black cover, and a piercing purple eye in the center. Legend has it that the Black Tome contains powerful spells that allow one to cast "magic." In reality, most of what's written inside is nonsensical teenage rambling, and reciting these so-called "incantations" does nothing at all. However, the claim that the Black Tome can grant magical powers isn't entirely false… which brings us to its abilities.
The Black Tome thrives off the power of belief. The more someone believes the Black Tome has powers, the more powerful it actually becomes. Stronger faith grants greater power to the Black Tome, and in turn, this power flows back to its believers: after reciting the incantations written in the Black Tome, believers can achieve nullification of some low threat anomalies. However, it is not the person reciting the spell who nullifies the Anomaly, but the Black Tome itself. The stronger the Black Tome becomes, the more powerful the targets it can nullify.
After first using an incantation from the Black Tome, another ability gradually manifests. It applies mental suggestion to users, causing them to treat their faith in the Black Tome as absolute truth. In pursuit of greater power, they are compelled to attract more people to believe in the Black Tome, eventually becoming a puppet with the sole purpose of spreading the Black Tome's faith. Those influenced and converted to believing in the Black Tome are also subjected to this blind faith, but do not gain the Black Tome's power. Additionally, the Black Tome sometimes uses its abilities to enslave and control low threat anomalies to serve itself.
When the Black Tome is opened by a non-believer, it generates an Anomalous Realm called the "Library," pulling the reader inside to face the Black Tome's true form. Its appearance within is a black humanoid figure, with the original book forming the head, surrounded by twisted limbs. Its behavior seems driven by wrath against non-believers, and it attempts to eliminate anyone who enters the Library. In battle, the Black Tome employs various magic-like methods, such as chains, flames, and beams appearing out of thin air, mostly stemming from believers' imagination of its power. Additionally, the Black Tome's close-range attacks using its own limbs should not be underestimated.
When the Black Tome is nullified, its mental influence disappears along with it. Based on current observations, no lingering aftereffects have been found. However, whether long-term belief in the Black Tome can cause permanent psychological distortion or even encroachment remains unknown. Anomalies that manipulate minds are undoubtedly among the most dangerous and insidious types.

Believing you are unique is a good thing, but being unique does not mean possessing extraordinary abilities, nor does it require pursuing great power. Ordinary yet unique… that probably sounds like something from a self-help book. However, if you equate "unique" with "powerful," you will embark on a tedious and endless path. The Black Tome exploits the confusion that people, especially young people, experience in understanding themselves, deceiving them in ways that are nearly impossible to guard against. I hope everyone can understand: we don't need to be powerful, we don't need to be geniuses, we don't need Esper Abilities to be irreplaceable individuals to those around us.

Anomaly Characteristics
· Appears as a black book. Its true form is a twisted humanoid object with a book for a head.
· Can absorb the power of "belief" to strengthen itself and apply mental suggestion to its believers.
· Can nullify or control low threat anomalies.
· The contents recorded in the book are mostly phrases born from adolescent fantasy and have no practical meaning.

Anomaly Nexus
The faith of believers is shaken. Suppressing and defeating the Black Tome within the Anomalous Realm can significantly weaken its mental influence on believers.

Risk Assessment
High hazard. Due to its inherent covertness, involvement of mental suggestion, and strong capacity for spreading and growth, it poses extreme potential danger to society. If discovered, it should be nullified immediately.

Containment/Guarantee Status
The only known specimen has been nullified.
